description: Issue #957: neutralizes the read-path credential masking in _DashboardController.Get by reverting `return Ok(DashboardCredentialMasking.MaskForRead(dashboard))` back to the pre-fix `return Ok(dashboard)`. CanAccess authorizes viewing dashboard content, not the credentials behind a REST widget's data source -- every widget's Source.RestOptions.Headers is exactly where an operator is documented to put Authorization/Cookie/API-key values. With this mutation applied, any viewer who merely passes CanAccess receives those header VALUES verbatim again, exactly as issue #957 originally reported (and the shipped viewer UI, framework_dashboard.js's DashboardManager._loadDashboard, actively fetches and holds that response). red_tests below cover: (1) a viewer directly observing an unmasked header value in the Get response, (2) a follow-up direct JsonFileDashboardService.GetAsync call after a Get, used as a premise check that the (now-absent) masking would have applied, and (3) the Update round-trip test's own premise check that a prior Get returned a masked sentinel -- all three fail because Get simply no longer masks anything. green_test is DashboardCredentialMaskingTests.MaskForRead_masks_header_values_but_preserves_keys, a pure unit test that calls DashboardCredentialMasking.MaskForRead directly (never through the controller) -- it stays green because the masking LOGIC itself is untouched by this mutation; only its invocation at the Get() call site was severed, which is exactly what this mutant is meant to isolate.

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against this branch's working tree (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) with the mutant patch applied, built and run exactly as run_mutant.py does (`dotnet build -c Release` then `dotnet test -c Release --no-restore --filter <red_test_filter>`) -- an earlier attempt (this file's first version) pinned the DEBUG-config failure text, which includes the FluentAssertions CallerArgumentExpression-captured subject text (e.g. 'Expected headers["Authorization"] to be ...'); under the RELEASE config run_mutant.py actually uses, two of the three tests instead show a generic type-name fallback ('Expected string to be ...') for that same subject text -- confirmed empirically to differ between configs for reasons not fully understood (not consistent even between structurally similar call sites: a third assertion with a similarly-long dotted/indexer chain kept its full expression text under the same Release build). The patterns above were rewritten to match only the STABLE tail every one of the three actual Release-mode failures share (verified by applying the patch manually and running `dotnet test -c Release --no-restore --filter <red_test_filter>` before touching this file again) -- 'Expected string to be "••••••••" with a length of 8, but "Bearer real-secret-should-never-reach-a-viewer" has a length of 46, differs near "Bea" (index 0).' for the first two, and the same tail (with the CallerArgumentExpression prefix intact) for the third. No other test in the same filter's TRX went red.
